meta.description: Multi-year governance structure and ideological scoring for Australian political parties, with international comparators. Latest scores are at the top level (for scatter plots); history arrays track changes over time (for timeline chart). Scores are approximate and deliberately coarse — see project page for full methodology.

left_right.description: Political ideology spectrum. -10 = far left (revolutionary socialist), -5 = social democratic, 0 = centre, +5 = conservative, +10 = far right.

internal_governance.description: Depth and genuineness of member control over party decisions. Composite of leadership selection, candidate preselection, policy platform approval, minority rights, and structural accountability mechanisms. 0 = leader-appointed, closed. 10 = full liquid/sortition/direct member democracy.

external_reform.description: Sustained external advocacy for governance reform — electoral reform, anti-corruption, transparency, accountability mechanisms. 0 = none or opposes reform. 10 = democracy reform is the party's primary platform and purpose.

notability.description: Rough public profile / electoral significance. Not a membership count (those are unreliable). 1 = marginal, virtually unknown. 5 = established minor party. 10 = government-forming major party.

parties.name: Australian Labor Party
parties.note: Faction-controlled preselections despite formal OMOV rules; weighted parliamentarian votes in some selections; internal reform pushes (Leigh, Faulkner) stalled.

history.note: Whitlam becomes leader. Pushes reform of party structure away from pure union control toward broader branch membership input. 36 faceless men image — federal conference still union-dominated but reform movement active.
Hawke government. Factional system formalised at national level (Centre-Left, Right, Left factions). Candidate selection largely determined by factional deals.
Rudd elected PM. Platform of internal party reform, greater member engagement. Some state branches experiment with OMOV preselections. Factional control persists federally.
Rudd rolled by Gillard in factional leadership coup. Factions reassert control. Internal reform agenda sidelined.
Rudd returns; pushes major internal reforms including stronger OMOV provisions for leadership and preselection. Faulkner's reform agenda gains brief traction.
Post-election loss. Reforms largely stalled. Factional duopoly re-established. Andrew Leigh later publicly criticises the 'duopoly' (2023).
National Anti-Corruption Commission Act enacted. External reform score rises, but exceptional-circumstances public-hearings threshold criticised by TI Australia and CPI.
Current. NACC has held 25+ private hearings and zero public hearings as of Dec 2025. Factional preselection control persists. Donation disclosure reforms legislated 2025.

parties.name: Liberal Party / Coalition
parties.note: Opposed real-time donation disclosure (2019); opposed truth-in-advertising bill; 2018/19 integrity commission proposal widely criticised as designed to hold only private hearings.

history.note: Founded by Menzies. Branch-based structure but elite-dominated; preselection controlled by state executives, not broad membership.
Fraser era. Centralised party control; branch stacking becomes entrenched practice in NSW and Queensland.
Howard era ends. Preselection remains faction/executive-controlled. No significant internal governance reform.
Federal director calls real-time donation disclosure 'too onerous'. Party opposes truth-in-advertising bill.
Current. No positive governance-reform record found. 2018/19 integrity commission proposal widely criticised as designed to hold only private hearings.

parties.name: Australian Greens
parties.note: Leadership not member-elected in all jurisdictions; varied preselection processes by state. Strong external record: 10-year federal anti-corruption campaign, truth-in-advertising bill, donation cap advocacy.

history.note: Founded from merger of state-based green parties. Decentralised federation model — state branches retain significant autonomy. Leadership and preselection processes vary by state. Early platform includes proportional representation and donation reform.
First federal lower house seat (Bandt, Melbourne). Federal anti-corruption body campaign begins to take shape. Donation reform advocacy intensifies.
NACC bill passes Senate with Greens amendments (inspector oversight powers). 10-year campaign delivers concrete win. Internal governance unchanged — leadership still not universally member-elected.

Current. Truth-in-advertising bill; Clean Up Politics campaign (donations caps, contractor donor bans) ongoing. Internal governance remains ~3 — the story is rising external reform advocacy against stable internal structure.

parties.name: Victorian Socialists
parties.note: Constitutional OMOV (adopted Jan 2024); competitive conference elections with minority faction platform rights; electorate-based branch structure. No external reform advocacy — revolutionary, not reformist (does not believe parliament can be meaningfully reformed under capitalism).

history.note: Estimate — prior to formal constitutional OMOV. Party had de facto democratic culture and volunteer-based structure, but formal member governance mechanisms not yet codified in constitution. Verify with party records.

Constitutional OMOV and party democracy adopted at Jan 2024 conference. Aims document adopted as part of new constitution: 'commitment to party democracy, freedom of debate and the principle of one member one vote.'

Electorate-based branch structures adopted at June 2025 conference. Competitive faction platform demonstrated: Communist Caucus ran alternative leadership slate, given platform time, lost at vote. 360 attendees.

Current. Reassessed from heartbeat 'too thin' after VS member counter-feedback. Deliberate non-reformist stance — external advocacy is building a democratic workers' movement, not patching parliament.

parties.name: One Nation
parties.note: Leader-dominated structure. AEC compliance action forced withdrawal of $800k+ contested election-spending claims (June 2026).

history.note: Initial scoring. AEC action June 2026.

parties.name: Jacqui Lambie Network
parties.note: Sustained integrity-body criticism since 2018; donations-disclosure bill on party site.

history.note: Initial scoring. Integrity-body advocacy since 2018.

parties.name: Katter's Australian Party
parties.note: Decentralisation calls and NQ partition referendum — policy positions, not sustained reform program.

history.note: Initial scoring.

parties.name: Pirate Party Australia
parties.note: Liquid democracy culture; merged into Fusion Party's federated structure 2021. Democracy and transparency reform is the party's reason for existing.

history.note: Initial scoring. Merged into Fusion 2021 but continues as distinct internal grouping.

parties.name: Australian Democrats
parties.note: Re-established. Advocates citizens' assembly for Vic upper house reform; proportional representation; evidence-based approach citing 2025 AES data.

history.note: Initial scoring. Re-established party with citizens' assembly and PR advocacy.

parties.name: Flux Party
parties.note: Issue-Based Direct Democracy (two-token economy, abstention-as-capital, proportional delegation). Deregistered. Included for historical comparison of governance innovation.

history.note: Registered with AEC. Issue-Based Direct Democracy as founding platform: two-token economy, abstention-as-capital, proportional delegation. Most sophisticated internal governance design of any Australian party.
Deregistered by AEC. IBDD mechanism unchanged throughout active period. Included for historical comparison of governance innovation.

parties.name: MiVote
parties.note: Four-destination policy model; research-to-voter information pipeline with university research, domain experts, advisory committees, and ethics committee sign-off; 60% supermajority threshold; mandatory mandate binding Senate candidates to member vote. Deregistered ~2019. Political sibling of Flux Party — both launched in the same period with complementary democracy-reform philosophies.

history.note: Founded by Adam Jacoby. Structured information pipeline, four-destination model, 60% supermajority, mandatory mandate. Constitutional requirement that elected senators vote according to aggregated member position.

Deregistered ~2019 without electing senators. MiVote Technologies continued in the UK. Included for historical comparison alongside Flux Party — political siblings with complementary governance designs.

parties.name: Your Party
parties.note: Sortition-selected founding conference delegates (via Sortition Foundation) — one of few parties globally using random selection for internal deliberative bodies. International comparator. General-purpose progressive platform alongside democratic reform.

history.note: Initial scoring. Founded 2025 with sortition-selected founding conference.
